front: Acetazolamide inhibits {{c1::carbonic anhydrase}} in the proximal tubule, causing a bicarbonate diuresis and a metabolic acidosis.

front: Addison disease mirrors Conn syndrome: aldosterone deficiency causes hyperkalemia, {{c1::metabolic acidosis}}, hyponatremia, and hypotension.

front: ADH increases water reabsorption by inserting:

why: Afferent vs efferent arteriole effects on GFR is a classic discrete tested every year

why: Osmolarity changes along the nephron is a standard tested sequence every year

front: Nephrotic versus nephritic syndrome: which loses protein massively, and which shows hematuria with hypertension?
why: Nephrotic vs nephritic syndrome is clinical pathology beyond the outline

why: GFR 125 mL/min / 180 L/day is the standard value used in renal calculations

why: Predicting hypokalemia/alkalosis/hypertension from aldosterone excess is a classic passage item

why: Creatinine clearance as the clinical GFR estimate is a common passage device
